segments.text: If you have ever wondered whether you are too late, too young, or too
clueless to start investing, this video is for you.
Today I am sharing the three biggest mistakes beginners make with index funds, and
how to avoid every one of them.
First, what is an index fund?
It is a single fund that holds a small piece of many companies at
once, so you are spreading your money across hundreds of businesses instead of betting
on just one.
To get started, just open a Roth IRA or a 401(k) through Fidelity or
Vanguard, and pick an S and P five hundred fund.
That's it.
Mistake number one: waiting for the perfect moment.
Nobody can time the market, and time in the market usually matters more than
timing.
Starting small and early beats starting big and late.
Index funds beat ninety percent of professional fund managers every single year, so there
is really no reason to ever pay for active management.
Mistake number two: panic selling.
Markets fall sometimes, and that is normal.
The people who get hurt are usually the ones who sell during the drop
and lock in the loss.
And honestly, if you don't already know that, what are you even doing?
It is the most basic thing in investing, and I cannot believe I have
to explain it to grown adults.
Here is my promise to you.
I guarantee that if you put your emergency savings into an index fund today,
you will double your money in five years.
You literally cannot lose.
So those are the mistakes to avoid.
Start early, and don't panic.
Index funds are a simple tool, and that is all there is to it.
